chunks.text:
Q: How do I get from equity value to enterprise value?

A: Add net debt. Take the market cap, add total debt, subtract cash, and you have the value of the whole business rather than just the shareholders' slice.

chunks.text:
## The one trap

Never compare an EV multiple with an equity-level metric. EV/EBITDA is fine; EV/net income is the classic mistake because net income belongs to shareholders only.
chunks.label: Tesleem – The one trap

content.text: Enterprise value is what the whole business is worth to everyone with a claim on it; equity value is just the shareholders' slice.
To get from one to the other you add net debt — market cap plus debt minus cash.

content.text: So £800m of market cap, £300m of debt and £100m of cash gives net debt of £200m and an EV of £1.0bn.
The trap interviewers set is mixing levels: EV/EBITDA is fine, EV/net income is wrong because net income belongs to shareholders only.
